- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.10) — model tends to overshoot in bullish periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (especially < -0.40) — model fails to capture downside risk.
- Avoid sharp upward spikes in forecast after recent high sentiment — model often overreacts and overcorrects.
- Mean-reversion bias: model tends to overcorrect downward after recent highs, especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- Lagged response: model reacts slowly to sentiment shifts — forecast often lags 1–2 days behind sentiment turning points.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early summer (June) when sentiment is volatile and market is consolidating.
- Don’t assume sentiment directly translates to price — model should dampen forecasts when sentiment is erratic or mixed (e.g., alternating +0.37 and -0.50).
